elements.evidence: The grant expressly states that the licence is “extending to Customer's affiliates.”

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly extends the licence “to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.”
The clause contains no perpetual duration for paid-up licences; instead, the licence may end upon termination of the Agreement.
The licence is only “irrevocable except upon termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 4,” so paid-up licences are not protected from revocation or termination in all cases.

elements.element: Subscription licences are terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Termination is tied generally to termination under Section 4. Section 4 is not provided, and the operative language does not limit termination to an uncured material breach.
Transferability is limited to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets, rather than successors generally.

elements.element: Affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Affiliates are covered automatically, without a notice condition, which necessarily includes coverage following written notice and is broader than the fallback.

elements.element: Licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits transfer “to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets.”

result.reason: The redline fully reaches the fallback but not the preferred position. It lacks perpetual protection for paid-up licences, does not make paid-up licences unconditionally irrevocable, does not restrict subscription termination to uncured material breach, and permits transfer only for specified M&A successors. It is not minimal because it adds contractor coverage and a general revocability provision beyond what was necessary for the completed fallback. The changes remain directed to licence scope and do not contradict the retained commercial terms.
